subject: Dedicated vs Private VPC \u001F data isolation follow-up

Subject: Post-call: dedicated vs private VPC - quick recap and next steps

Hi Alice - great to meet today. Quick recap from our discovery and the follow-ups we promised: 

- Summary of need: FinSecure is evaluating a deployment that provides strict data isolation for customer PII and ML inputs/outputs. You summarized two primary options you want us to validate: Dedicated (reserved GPU capacity) vs Private (VPC or on-prem).
- Primary requirements called out on the call: no shared-tenant compute for inference, customer-managed encryption keys (KMS/HSM), audit logs retained for at least 1 year, and the ability to limit telemetry/model usage metadata leaving your VPC.
- Questions we promised to clarify: differences in control plane exposure between Dedicated and Private, how customer-managed KMS works in each mode, and a high-level timeline for a pilot.

Next steps I propose: 
1) I'll send a short one-page comparison + the security questionnaire (attached).
2) Schedule a technical deep-dive with our infra lead (cc'd Mateo) and your security/infra folks next week - can you share availability?
3) If the comparison looks good, we'll scope a Q3 pilot (approx 4-6 weeks).

Attachments: Redwood_Dedicated_vs_Private_VPC_Summary.pdf, FinSecure_Security_Questionnaire.xlsx

Thanks - I'll follow up once I have availability from Mateo.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Thanks, Marissa - appreciate the summary. A few clarifications from our security team before the deep-dive: 

- Isolation: we require no shared compute with other Redwood customers for inference runs that process PII. Is Dedicated single-tenant at the host level or just reserved capacity?
- KMS/HSM: keys must be customer-managed. Can Redwood integrate with our on-prem HSM or a customer KMS in cloud (e.g., AWS KMS with BYOK)?
- Telemetry & logs: we want the ability to opt out of model telemetry and have full control over audit/log export into our SIEM.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Bennett <alice.bennett@finsecure.com>, Procurement <procurement@finsecure.com>
Cc: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-10T11:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: dedicated vs private VPC - quick recap and next steps

Hi Alice / team - thanks for the clear questions. Short answers up front, followed by the attachments and proposed next steps.

1) Isolation - Dedicated vs Private
  - Dedicated: reserved, single-tenant GPU pools (compute isolation) with our managed control plane. The inference servers are dedicated to the customer, so there is no co-located inference compute from other customers on the same GPU hosts. However, control plane operations (job routing, autoscaling signals, metadata indexing) are handled by Redwood's control plane unless you choose Private.
  - Private (VPC / on-prem): full private deployment where the control plane can be customer-managed (VPC peering or on-prem package). This configuration removes dependency on Redwood's shared control plane and is the stronger isolation model for regulated workloads.

2) KMS/HSM
  - Dedicated: supports customer-managed KMS in cloud (BYOK) for encryption at-rest; HSM integration limited to supported cloud KMS providers (we can route key requests to customer KMS).
  - Private: supports both cloud BYOK and on-prem HSM integrations; keys can remain in-customer and never transit Redwood-managed KMS.

3) Telemetry & logs
  - We can provide opts to disable model telemetry and route logs/audit events directly to your SIEM via secure forwarders in both Dedicated and Private, but Private gives you full control over log collection endpoints and retention policies.

4) Compliance artifacts
  - Attaching a high-level one-pager and our standard security questionnaire (attached). SOC 2 report and pen-test summaries are available under NDA - happy to provide redacted copies once we have a mutual NDA or appropriate DPA in place.

5) Timeline / pilot
  - Dedicated pilot: typically 2-3 weeks to stand up reserved capacity + config + basic integrations.
  - Private pilot (VPC-managed): typically 4-6 weeks (networking, KMS/HSM, audit/alerting routes). On-prem deployments add additional lead time depending on procurement and hardware.

Next steps I recommend: 
- Confirm availability for a technical deep-dive Tuesday/Wednesday afternoon PT - Mateo (infra lead) will present deployment options and integration details.
- If Procurement wants TCO estimates beforehand, we can produce a short mem with ballpark numbers for Dedicated vs Private (I'll loop in our pricing lead).

Attachments: Redwood_Dedicated_vs_Private_VPC_Summary.pdf, FinSecure_Security_Questionnaire.xlsx

Best,
Marissa
